q: The Shards of the Cosmere are pieces of which ancient being?
explain: Adonalsium was broken in the Shattering, and its power was divided among the Shards.

q: How many Shards was Adonalsium split into?
explain: Each of the sixteen Shards embodies a single Intent, such as Honor, Ruin or Endowment.

q: The Almighty worshipped in the Vorin religion is actually which Shard?
explain: Dalinar learns that the Almighty of Vorinism was Honor, and that he is dead.

q: Which Shard was responsible for the death of Honor?
explain: Odium Splintered Honor before the events of The Way of Kings.

q: Which two Shards worked together to create humankind on Scadrial?
explain: Ruin agreed in exchange for being allowed to destroy the world later, but Preservation betrayed and imprisoned him at great cost to himself.

q: Stormlight is the Investiture of which Shard?
explain: Each Shard on Roshar has its own Light, and Stormlight is Honor's.

q: Who takes up Preservation's power to fight Ruin directly?
explain: Vin and Ruin destroyed each other in their final clash.

q: Atium turns out to be the concentrated body of which Shard?
explain: Ruin hid his body as atium, which was mined in the Pits of Hathsin.

q: On Roshar, what is the Cognitive Realm commonly called?
explain: Jasnah and Shallan can glimpse and even slip into Shadesmar through Soulcasting.
source: The Way of Kings; Words of Radiance

q: The Physical and Cognitive Realms are two of the three Realms. What is the third?
explain: The Spiritual Realm holds a thing's ideal form and is outside time and space.

q: What position does Hoid hold at King Elhokar's court?
explain: As Wit he insults courtiers for a living, yet keeps his true purpose hidden.

q: Which worldhopper narrates Tress of the Emerald Sea?
explain: Hoid tells the story of Tress, a young woman of the island world Lumar.

q: Which sentient sword from Nalthis ends up on Roshar?
explain: Nightblood was Awakened on Nalthis with the Command to destroy evil.

q: Which Rosharan carries a sentient black sword from Nalthis in Oathbringer?
explain: Szeth trains with the Skybreakers under Nale while bearing the sword.

q: Which secret society, through its agent Mraize, recruits Shallan?
explain: In Words of Radiance, Mraize has Shallan, disguised as Veil, spy on Amaram's Sons of Honor.

q: Which was the first Cosmere novel to be published?
explain: Elantris came out in 2005, set on the planet Sel.

q: What is the general Cosmere term for the power of the Shards in all its forms?
explain: Stormlight, Breath and the Dor are all forms of Investiture on their respective worlds.

q: What makes up the 'ocean' of the Cognitive Realm on Roshar?
explain: Each bead represents an object in the Physical Realm, and touching one reveals its nature.

q: The Stormfather is a remnant of which Shard?
explain: After Honor's death, the Stormfather retained fragments of his power and memories.

q: Which worldhopper is the protagonist of The Sunlit Man?
explain: Nomad keeps jumping between worlds to escape the Night Brigade.

q: Who took up both Ruin and Preservation to become Harmony?
explain: Sazed, as Harmony, is worshipped by the people of Elendel in the second Mistborn era.

q: What is a Sliver?
a: Someone who once held a Shard and then let it go
wrong: Someone who currently holds a Shard's power
A spren bonded to a Herald
explain: The Lord Ruler became a Sliver after briefly holding Preservation's power.

q: Which Shard is invested on Nalthis, the world of Warbreaker?
explain: Endowment gives each person a single Breath and sends the Returned back to life.

q: Allomancy draws its power from which Shard?
explain: The metals only act as a catalyst for Preservation's power, while Hemalurgy is tied to Ruin.

q: In The Lost Metal, the god Trell is revealed to be a guise of which Shard?
explain: Harmony tells Wax that Autonomy acts through independent avatars, and Trell is one of them.

q: In The Lost Metal, which group led by Kelsier invites Marasi to join it?
explain: Marasi works alongside offworld Ghostblood agents but turns down Kelsier's offer.

q: In Mistborn: Secret History, in which Realm does the protagonist linger after his death?
explain: He refuses to pass into the Beyond and survives as a Cognitive Shadow.

q: Which worldhopper is the in-world author of the planetary essays in Arcanum Unbounded?
explain: Khriss is a scholar of the Cosmere who studies its worlds and magic systems.

q: From which planet does the scholar Khriss come?
explain: Khriss is a Darksider who travels to the Dayside of her world in White Sand.

q: Which two Shards were Splintered on Sel?
explain: Their scattered power fuels the Dor, the source of Selish magic.

q: In Warbreaker, which god summons Hoid to the Court of Gods to tell stories?
explain: Hoid recounts the history of the first Returned and the origin of the God Kings.

q: What musical instrument does Hoid leave with Kaladin?
explain: Hoid plays it while telling the story of Derethil and the Wandersail, then tells Kaladin to keep it.

q: Which spren does Hoid find in Kholinar and later bond?
explain: Hoid bonds the Cryptic Design and, through that bond, becomes a Lightweaver.

q: What is the name of Hoid's homeworld?
explain: Yolen is where Adonalsium was Shattered, and is the setting of the planned Dragonsteel books.

q: Under what name does Vasher work as a swordmaster on Roshar?
explain: Zahel trains Adolin, and his speech hints at the colors and Breath of Nalthis.
source: Words of Radiance; Words of Brandon

q: What is a place where a Shard's power pools and links the Realms, allowing travel between them?
explain: Worldhoppers often use Perpendicularities to enter and leave the Cognitive Realm.

q: On Scadrial, which place is Preservation's Perpendicularity?
explain: In Secret History, the novella's dead protagonist spends years beside the Well of Ascension.

q: What keeps Odium from leaving the Rosharan system?
explain: Odium seeks a contest of champions as a way to escape this binding.

q: Who does Dalinar learn is the true identity of the old woman of the Valley?
explain: Cultivation lives in the Valley alongside the Nightwatcher, a powerful spren.

q: How does Odium describe himself to Dalinar?
explain: Odium insists he embodies every passion, not only hatred.

q: In Rhythm of War, with which weapon is Odium's Vessel killed?
explain: Nightblood's hunger for Investiture let it destroy the Vessel of a Shard.

q: Who was the original Vessel of Odium?
explain: Rayse held Odium for millennia, until he was killed at the end of Rhythm of War.

q: Who was the original Vessel of Ruin?
explain: Holding Ruin for millennia gradually twisted Ati's mind toward its Intent.

q: Who is the Vessel of the Shard Autonomy?
explain: Little is known about Bavadin, one of the most elusive Vessels in the Cosmere.

q: Which Shard did Odium mortally wound in the Threnodite system?
explain: Ambition survived that clash but was later Splintered somewhere else.

q: Which worldhopper collects maps and artifacts for his employer and annotates the charts?
explain: Nazh's handwritten notes appear on several of the maps and illustrations in the books.

q: The Elantrian Galladon is a member of which worldhopper society?
explain: The Seventeenth Shard opposes meddling with the Shards and their worlds.

q: In which region of Roshar is Cultivation's Perpendicularity?
explain: The Unkalaki tell of a sacred lake there that leads to the realm of the gods.

q: Who is the masked worldhopper who serves as Mraize's babsk?
explain: Iyatil always keeps her face hidden behind a mask.

q: Which offworld Ghostblood agent uses soulstamps in The Lost Metal?
explain: Soulstamps are a Selish art, the same one practised in The Emperor's Soul.

q: Which planet of the Rosharan system do Rosharans call Damnation?
explain: Braize, the cold third planet of the system, is where Odium is bound and where the Heralds returned between Desolations.
source: Arcanum Unbounded, The Rosharan System; Rhythm of War

q: From which planet of the Rosharan system did the humans of Roshar originally flee?
explain: Humans destroyed much of Ashyn with their powers and came to Roshar as refugees.
source: Oathbringer (Eila Stele); Arcanum Unbounded, The Rosharan System

q: What does a Feruchemist store in a duralumin metalmind?
explain: Duralumin stores Connection, the Spiritual link to people and places; aluminum stores Identity, chromium Fortune and nicrosil Investiture.
source: The Bands of Mourning, Ars Arcanum

q: What is the name of the Light that is the Investiture of Cultivation?
explain: Lifelight is Cultivation's Light; combined with Stormlight it produces the Sibling's Towerlight.

q: From which planet does the worldhopper Nazh come?
explain: Nazh is a native of Threnody, the world of the Forests of Hell.

q: Which city in the Cognitive Realm is a gathering place for worldhoppers from many planets?
explain: Silverlight lies in the Cognitive Realm and serves as a meeting point for worldhoppers and scholars of the Realms.

q: According to Nikli in Dawnshard, the Dawnshards were eventually used to do what?
explain: The Dawnshards are the four primal Commands that created all things, later turned against Adonalsium itself.

q: The Sleepless are hive minds made up of swarms of which small creatures?
explain: A Sleepless spreads its mind across countless hordelings and can replace lost ones, letting it live for ages.

q: What was the name of the Vessel of Preservation?
explain: Leras sacrificed much of his power to imprison Ruin, leaving himself near death.

q: The Sibling, the spren of Urithiru, is born of which two Shards?
explain: The Sibling harmonizes the rhythms of Honor and Cultivation to produce Towerlight.

q: In Wind and Truth, Honor and Odium are joined into a single new Shard. What is it called?
explain: Odium's Vessel absorbs Honor's power, and the combined Shard is called Retribution.

q: In Wind and Truth, who briefly takes up the power of Honor?
explain: Dalinar ascends as Honor's Vessel and then renounces his oaths, releasing the Shard.

q: In what role does Hoid appear in Luthadel in The Final Empire?
explain: Hoid sells information in Luthadel, and Kelsier is among those who consult him.

q: Hoid makes a brief appearance in The Alloy of Law, dressed as a beggar. At what event?
explain: Hoid comes to the Yomen wedding reception to congratulate the couple, shortly before the Vanishers attack.

q: In Secret History, what does Hoid swallow in the chamber of the Well of Ascension?
explain: No one can stop Hoid, who consumes the lerasium and leaves the chamber.

q: What kind of creature is Mraize's green pet bird?
explain: Mraize's bird is an aviar, one of the talent-granting birds of First of the Sun.
source: Rhythm of War; Wind and Truth

q: Shallan overhears Mraize say that some pages must be brought to his master. Which name does he use?
explain: Thaidakar leads Mraize's secret society, rivals of Restares and the Sons of Honor.

q: How does Hoid illustrate the history of Hallandren when he tells it at the Court of Gods?
a: By dropping colored sands and dusts
explain: As Hoid speaks he lets sands, dusts and small objects fall, forming shapes on the floor.

q: Which story does Wit tell Kaladin when he finds him in a nightmare in Rhythm of War?
wrong: The Boy Who Stole the Wind
explain: With his Cryptic creating illusions, Wit tells of a dog who wanted to become a dragon.

q: In Secret History, what nickname does the protagonist give Preservation?
explain: He befriends the dying Preservation and calls him Fuzz.

q: In Secret History, what does Nazh give the protagonist before they part ways?
explain: Nazh also points him toward the Ire, and he later uses the knife to smash their device and take up Preservation's power.

q: What do the Eelakin call the spacefaring visitors who sell them technology?
explain: Dusk distrusts the Ones Above, even though he bought accurate sea maps from them.

q: What is the god metal associated with Odium called?
explain: Presumably named after Odium's original Vessel, raysium has long been used by Odium's forces in their weapons.

q: What symbol must every member of the Ghostbloods have tattooed?
explain: Jasnah later finds this symbol tattooed on the arm of a would-be assassin.

q: According to Arcanum Unbounded, how do people on Ashyn now gain magical powers?
explain: After the cataclysm, Ashyn's magic became tied to illnesses.

q: Which worldhopper took Sigzil on as an apprentice Worldsinger?
explain: Sigzil travelled with his master Hoid, training as a Worldsinger, before ending up in Bridge Four.
source: The Way of Kings; Words of Radiance

q: In Secret History, which crew member is freed from Ruin's control in Urteau and then visited in a dream?
explain: In that dream, Spook is told to warn Vin about people pierced by metal.

q: In Dawnshard, what kind of being is Nikli, Rysn's attendant?
explain: Nikli is a Sleepless swarm skilled at impersonating humans, set to guard the secrets of the hidden Aimian city.

q: What policy does the Shard of Khriss's homeworld impose on it?
wrong: Rule by a council of worldhoppers
explain: The Shard keeps that world cut off while meddling elsewhere, so worldhoppers born there cannot return home.

q: In Tress of the Emerald Sea, which Selish magic does the narrator use to block the Sorceress's curse aimed at Tress?
explain: The Sorceress was casting her curse with AonDor, and the narrator burst into her tower and blocked it with an Aon of his own.

q: In Elantris, what does Hoid help Sarene do?
explain: Late in the novel, Hoid quietly helps Sarene get weapons into the city of Elantris.

q: Which of these beings belongs to Elantris rather than to Mistborn: The Final Empire?
explain: Seons are the floating balls of light of Elantris; kandra, mistwraiths and Steel Inquisitors all appear in The Final Empire.
source: Elantris, ch. 1; Mistborn: The Final Empire, ch. 8 (mistwraith); Coppermind: Mistwraith

q: Which of these characters belongs to Mistborn: The Final Empire rather than to Elantris?
explain: Clubs is the Smoker and carpenter of the thieving crew; Mareshe, Ahan and Lukel are characters from Elantris.

q: Which of these titles belongs to the Steel Ministry of The Final Empire rather than to the Derethi hierarchy of Elantris?
explain: Obligators are the priests of the Steel Ministry; arteth, grador and odiv are positions in the Derethi chain of command.

q: Which of these characters belongs to Elantris rather than to Mistborn: The Final Empire?
explain: Eondel is an Arelene noble and soldier who allies with Sarene; Dockson, Camon and Ham are characters from The Final Empire.

q: Which of these places appears in Mistborn: The Final Empire rather than in Elantris?
explain: Fellise is the small town outside the imperial capital where the Renoux mansion stands; Ake, Ato and Toa are the outer cities around Elantris.
